comments.content: The `validateAuthState` method no longer calls `resetAuthNonce()` after validation. This breaks the one-time-use property of the nonce, allowing replay attacks. The nonce should be invalidated after successful validation.

The nonce is now generated once in the constructor and never changes. This means the same nonce is reused across all authentication attempts, which defeats the purpose of a state parameter (CSRF protection). A new nonce should be generated for each auth flow initiation.

`createAuthRequest` no longer generates a new nonce when starting an auth flow. It reuses the static nonce from the constructor. This allows an attacker to capture a valid state value and reuse it. Move the nonce generation inside this method (when not authenticated) to ensure a fresh nonce per flow.

The state mismatch handling now prompts the user to continue anyway, which undermines CSRF protection. If the state doesn't match, the request should be rejected outright. The comment mentions 'signins initiated from outside the extension (e.g. Cline web)' — if cross-origin flows are needed, implement a proper PKCE or pre-registered redirect URI flow instead of weakening state validation.
